skill.description: Create a reviewed talking-head video package by transcribing speech, detecting likely mistakes, collecting edit choices in a local review page, and producing a cut video with corrected subtitles.
skill.summary: Prepare talking-head footage for editing with transcription, review, cutting, and subtitle outputs.
skill.author: chengfeng / AI产品自由

security_audit.summary: The skill is a local video transcription and editing workflow, but it executes FFmpeg and shell commands using runtime paths. The review server has unauthenticated wildcard-CORS endpoints and unsafely maps URL paths to local files; the Volcengine helper also reads an API key and sends audio to the configured provider. Many scanner findings are benign JavaScript template literals, fixed local workflow paths, or documentation heuristics.

remediation.issue: Shell commands interpolate runtime filenames and generated values.
remediation.suggestion: Replace execSync shell strings with execFileSync or spawn using argument arrays. Validate filenames, reject control characters, and never generate executable shell scripts from untrusted values.

remediation.issue: The review server exposes files and cut actions without access controls.
remediation.suggestion: Bind only to 127.0.0.1, remove wildcard CORS, authenticate state-changing endpoints, enforce request-size limits, and resolve requested files against an allowlisted directory before serving them.

remediation.issue: The transcription helper reads a local API key and uploads audio to Volcengine.
remediation.suggestion: Document the external data transfer clearly, restrict .env permissions, avoid logging secret-bearing responses, and let users explicitly confirm the provider and audio upload.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated server exposes local files and editing actions
semantic_findings.description: The review server accepts arbitrary URL paths by prefixing them with a dot, without normalizing or restricting traversal. It also exposes save and cut endpoints without authentication and permits every origin through CORS, enabling a local or network caller to overwrite selection data and trigger video processing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The server explicitly enables wildcard CORS, has no authentication checks, and maps request URLs directly to filesystem paths. These combined behaviors create a clear local file exposure and unauthorized action risk.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded request bodies allow resource exhaustion
semantic_findings.description: The save-selection and cut endpoints append every incoming chunk to an in-memory string without a size limit or timeout. A client can consume process memory before JSON parsing or file writing occurs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both endpoint handlers concatenate request chunks with no length check. This is a direct memory exhaustion condition when the server is reachable.

content.value_statement: Talking-head footage can take time to review for pauses, repeated words, and speaking errors. This skill creates a review workflow, cuts approved segments, and prepares subtitle files for the edited video.
actual_capabilities: Extracts and transcribes speech from a supplied video using the configured Volcengine service.
Builds word-timestamp data and flags candidate filler words, repetitions, silence, and incomplete speech.
Generates a local browser review page for selecting segments to remove.
Cuts approved segments with FFmpeg and produces a new video file.
Retranscribes the edited video and writes draft SRT subtitle output.
limitations: Requires FFmpeg, Node.js, and access to a configured Volcengine transcription account.
Uploads audio to Volcengine when using its transcription script.
Automatic deletion suggestions require human review before cutting.
The included local review server is not designed for shared or public networks.

use_cases.title: Review a creator recording
use_cases.description: Identify pauses and speech mistakes before preparing a cleaner talking-head source video.

use_cases.title: Prepare training footage
use_cases.description: Review a recorded lesson, approve removals, and create subtitles for a refined training clip.

use_cases.title: Process interview segments
use_cases.description: Create a reviewable transcript and cut selected disfluencies from an interview recording.

prompt_templates.title: Start with one video
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare this talking-head video for editing. Create the review package and explain what I need to approve before cutting.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on speaking mistakes
prompt_templates.prompt: Transcribe this video and flag likely filler words, repetitions, long pauses, and incomplete sentences for my review.

prompt_templates.title: Create an approved cut
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my approved deletion selections to cut the video. Then generate draft subtitles from the edited video.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a delivery package
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare this recording as an editing package. Keep the original source, create a review page, apply only my confirmed cuts, and report all output files.

output_examples.input: Prepare a five-minute product explanation video for review.
output: A local review page with suggested segments to inspect.
A word-timestamp transcript and an approved-cut video after confirmation.
Draft subtitles generated from the edited video.

output_examples.input: Remove only the pauses and repeated phrases that I confirm.
output: A list of confirmed removal segments.
A cut video that preserves unconfirmed speech.
A subtitle file aligned to the cut video.

best_practices: Review every automatic deletion suggestion before starting the cut.
Keep original media and generated outputs in a dedicated project folder.
Confirm that you are permitted to upload the recording to the selected transcription provider.
anti_patterns: Do not expose the local review server to a shared or public network.
Do not treat draft subtitles as final without checking names, numbers, and timing.
Do not delete the original video before reviewing the cut output.

faq.question: What files does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates review assets, transcript data, a cut video after approval, and draft subtitle files.

faq.question: Does it cut video automatically?
faq.answer: It suggests segments, but the workflow expects you to review and confirm removals before cutting.

faq.question: What software is required?
faq.answer: You need Node.js and FFmpeg. The Volcengine workflow also needs an API key and network access.

faq.question: Does transcription leave my computer?
faq.answer: Yes. The Volcengine helper uploads audio to Volcengine for transcription.

faq.question: Can I use it for public or shared review pages?
faq.answer: No. The included server is intended only for local use and should not be exposed publicly.

faq.question: Are subtitles final-ready?
faq.answer: No. They are draft outputs and should be checked for accuracy and timing before publishing.
